misconceptions.description: Listing only the obvious stakeholders (teachers, students, vendor) and missing the silent or most-affected parties
misconceptions.trigger: learner names buyers and direct users but omits English learners, parents, or the data officer
misconceptions.feedback: Ask who is most affected yet least consulted. The silent stakeholder, often the most-affected group, must appear on the map.

misconceptions.description: Assuming all stakeholders want the same thing because the tool is described as helpful
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes that a tool 'helps everyone' without naming any conflicting interest
misconceptions.feedback: Name at least one genuine conflict. Vendor adoption, teacher time, and student equity often pull in different directions.

misconceptions.description: Treating the AI vendor as a neutral service rather than a stakeholder with its own data and adoption interests
misconceptions.trigger: learner leaves the vendor off the stakeholder map or lists it without an interest
misconceptions.feedback: The vendor is a stakeholder. Name its interest in data and adoption, since that interest can shape the design more than student needs.
